## Per-file results, copy and export

- A blueprint has 13+ script files (a .gs and an .html per tool, plus appsscript.json). The Update
  Timeline lists, under each document, one line per file: updated or unchanged, with the file's
  "Last updated on YYYY-MM-DD at HH:MM TZ" stamp read from the top of the file. All main-repo code
  files carry it; appsscript.json cannot (JSON has no comments); Code10.gs and Sidebar10.html in the
  private repo have none yet.
- "Updated" vs "Unchanged": Google replaces every file on each upload, so the app compares
  content to say which files actually changed.
- **Copy results** (tab-separated, pastes as a table) and **Export to Google Sheet** (a new tab in
  the log sheet named "Update YYYY-MM-DD HH.MM"). Google Sheet chosen over CSV: the organisation
  works in Google, and a Sheet can be shared, filtered and sorted without a download/upload step.
- Export columns, one row per file per document: uploaded (date and time), Google account,
  document name, document address, script source (repo and branch), file, file's "Last updated"
  stamp, result (Updated / Unchanged / Failed: reason), backup link.
- Check also shows stamps ("document has 2026-09-12, Main has 2026-09-25") but decides by content.

## Choosing where each document updates from (by tool)

- Each checked blueprint gets **Update from: Main · Experimental** (Custom appears when any tool
  is changed). It sets the starting choice for every tool; the main screen's "For blueprints"
  source is the starting choice for every document. The row's tick box still decides whether the
  document is included, so there is no "Don't update" option.
- The **Tools and files** table is grouped by tool, not by file: a tool's .gs and .html files
  always move together. Each tool has one pick-one choice: Keep (or Don't add) · Main ·
  Experimental. A source without the tool is greyed out. Files not in GitHub get Keep · Remove.
- Safe defaults: a tool that is newer in the document than in the chosen source starts on Keep.
- Dependency warnings with one-click fixes (only fixes that actually clear the problem are
  offered). A document with an unfixed warning is skipped. Known dependencies: Code.gs builds the
  menu (must list every tool present); appsscript.json holds permissions (Create Video List needs
  Google Sheets access). The list of dependencies will be confirmed from the code when building.
- Confirm screen, Update Timeline and export all show which source each file came from.

## appsscript.json

- Checked like every other file, by content, with its own "Permissions" row. The row says in
  plain words what each source would add or remove (e.g. "Experimental adds Google Sheets access").
- Date stamp: JSON has no comments. To test in Phase 0 whether Google accepts an extra field in
  the manifest. If it does not, the stamp goes on a line in Code.gs's header
  ("appsscript.json last updated on ..."), and the app can also date it from the GitHub commit
  that last changed it. To be added when building (the user asked for it).

## Naming and layout changes (after mockup review)

- Repos are called **Main Repo** (blueprint-tools-script) and **Experimental Repo**
  (blueprint-tools-script-private) everywhere. The branch name "(main)" is no longer shown: it
  repeated the word Main and confused the two meanings. Branch only shown if it is ever not main.
- The **Script source** card on the main screen is removed: the per-document "Update from" choice
  replaces it. Every document starts on the Main Repo. A bar at the top of the list after Check,
  "Update every ticked blueprint from: Main Repo · Experimental Repo", switches many at once.
  The Initial setup card is renamed **GitHub repos** (Main Repo, Experimental Repo, Quiz Repo).
- "Log (Google Sheet)" renamed **Update history (Google Sheet)**: the permanent record, one row per
  document per update, plus a tab for each "Export to Google Sheet".
- Per-document toggle: once tools are mixed, the Update from buttons fade and the line says
  "Mixed". They stay clickable as a one-click reset (not disabled). When the choices again match
  one repo (counting tools where both repos are identical, and safe Keep defaults), that repo's
  button lights up again.

## Open links in the Drive picker

- Every file in the picker (and in step 2, "What's inside the folders") has an **Open ↗** link that
  opens it in the default web browser (Drive gives each file's web address; Electron's
  shell.openExternal opens it). Read-only: it does not tick, untick or change anything, and the
  picker stays open. The link is separate from the file name so clicking the name still ticks.
- The folder action is renamed **Look inside ›** so "Open" always means "open in the browser".
